title: Go SDK streaming iterator: coordinated backoff, deadline propagation, and user ergonomics playbook
creator: Evan Rodriguez
description:
Problem: Users of the Go SDK frequently run into tricky behaviors when combining context timeouts/cancellations with long-lived streaming RPCs. Symptoms include leaked goroutines, inconsistent backoff across reconnect attempts, and surprising client-visible latency spikes when upstream transient errors occur.

Goal: Define and implement a robust, well-documented streaming iterator pattern in the Go SDK that: (1) consistently propagates context deadlines and cancellations across all internal goroutines and network calls, (2) centralizes backoff and retry coordination so per-message retries don't conflict with stream-level reconnect logic, (3) provides ergonomic APIs and a short set of examples demonstrating best practices for application developers, and (4) adds test coverage and observability for production debugging.

Scope: library-level API additions/changes, internal streaming session manager, new examples in examples/streaming, integration tests against the runtime test harness, and updated docs in the SDK README and playbooks. Not in scope: changing server-side protocol semantics or adding resumable checkpoint tokens to the protocol (future follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: The SDK exposes a StreamIterator abstraction with clear Close/Context semantics documented.
Context deadlines cancel all internal work (connection, read loop, prefetch) and do not leak goroutines after Close/timeout.
Backoff & retry coordinator ensures only one reconnection loop runs per stream and obeys global per-request circuit-breaker constraints.
Examples show common patterns: short client deadlines, streaming to completion with long-lived contexts, and cooperative shutdown on signals.
Integration tests simulate transient server errors, verify reconnect behavior, and assert no goroutine leaks (using goroutine count heuristics).
Telemetry emits reconnection_attempt, backoff_delay_ms, stream_closed_reason (user_cancel / context_deadline / server_error).
implementation_notes: Introduce internal streamManager struct that owns the connection, read loop, prefetch buffer, and a single reconnect coordinator goroutine.
streamManager receives cancellation via a single context created per StreamIterator; user-provided context is used to derive it (ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parentCtx)).
Reconnection/backoff uses exponential jittered backoff with a max cap; implement a token-based circuit-breaker for too-frequent restarts to protect the runtime.

Per-message timeouts: do NOT spawn independent per-message contexts that can outlive the streamManager; instead use per-API call deadlines that are checked inline and result in an immediate return for that message while leaving stream state intact.
Make Close() idempotent and synchronous (Close blocks until internal goroutines have exited) to match user expectations and make teardown deterministic in tests.
Expose a BlockingClose(ctx) helper that accepts a context for callers that want bounded wait on Close, to avoid blocking forever in bad network conditions.
Metrics: increment metric labels for reconnection attempts, last_error, and 'stream_lifetime_seconds'. Attach span events for reconnects + backoff durations.
Errors: wrap internal transient error reasons with sentinel types so calling code and tests can assert on 'server_error' vs 'client_cancel' vs 'deadline'.

Examples: create three short examples and place under examples/streaming/ -- (1) short-lived request with timeout, (2) long-lived chat consumer with graceful shutdown on SIGTERM, (3) resiliency demo showing backoff behavior after injected transient failures.
steps: Design doc: outline APIs and failure modes (link in attachments).
Prototype streamManager and iterator in an internal branch; add unit tests for cancellation propagation.
Add integration tests using runtime test harness (inject transient errors, enforce goroutine thresholds).
Write examples and docs; sanity review by DX and SDK owners.
Code review, iterate on feedback, merge and cut go-sdk-1.9 release with migration notes.
decisions: Prefer a single reconnect coordinator per stream over ad-hoc per-reader reconnects to avoid duplicate connections and competing backoffs.
Keep API surface minimal: StreamIterator.Next(ctx) + StreamIterator.Close() + StreamIterator.BackingInfo() rather than introducing many variants.
Do not modify server protocol for resumability in this iteration; add a follow-up ticket for checkpoint tokens if needed.
